extraction.name: XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations across four task families: speech recognition, speech translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval, covering 102 languages and multiple speech domains.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is built from several publicly available speech datasets and one newly built dataset (Fleurs). For Fleurs-ASR, the authors used 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest public sets in 102 languages, collected between one and three recordings per sentence, and created new train/dev/test splits. Other benchmark components use MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-14.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Fleurs is described as complete at more than 97%, and the authors note that some slight improvements and changes may be made in a second version of the dataset, such as missing recordings or replaced low-quality recordings.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public speech datasets and corpora: FLoRes dev/devtest sentences for Fleurs, Librivox audiobooks for MLS, European Parliament speech for VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2 speech translation corpus, and MINDS-14 spoken intent classification data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Fleurs-ASR, the authors collected one to three recordings per sentence and built new train-dev-test splits with 1509 train, 150 dev, and 350 test sentences. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For retrieval, the pool of transcription candidates was augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The benchmark uses official or newly constructed train/dev/test splits, multilingual fine-tuning, and task-specific evaluation setups. For Fleurs-LangID, the same splits as ASR are used. For retrieval, embeddings are computed for dev/test sets and nearest-neighbor search is performed over ground-truth transcriptions plus additional Wikipedia/CommonCrawl sentences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper does not describe a separate human annotation protocol for labels beyond using existing dataset annotations/transcriptions and, for Fleurs, collecting speech recordings for parallel sentences. For speech classification and retrieval, the benchmark uses existing labels/transcriptions from the source datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: HuggingFace platform is mentioned for dataset access and fine-tuning scripts; no annotation platform is specified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For speech classification, the authors recommend reporting the average result over 5 random seeds after hyperparameter tuning to reduce variance. For Fleurs-LangID, they note that speakers differ between train and dev/test sets and that overfitting on speaker identity should be avoided.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made accessible through HuggingFace. The authors state that updates will be made on their platform, that some slight improvements and changes may be done in a second version of Fleurs, and that more details will be added on the XTREME-S dataset card. Test sets are open-source and submissions are double-checked through prediction submission.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes language, geography, and speech-related attributes; the paper also discusses speaker differences between train and dev/test sets for Fleurs-LangID. No explicit collection of other sensitive attributes is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by the need to make speech technology available in all languages, especially for under-represented languages, to give speakers an equal voice on the Internet and improve access to speech technology for low-resource communities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that results are much better on Western European languages than on Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages, partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data in Western European languages. It also notes that speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting because of the discrepancy between rich input signals and small label sets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: XTREME-S is focused on linguistic aspects of speech and does not evaluate nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects such as those relevant to speech synthesis or voice conversion. The benchmark is not saturated by current baselines, and the authors note gaps across geographical groups. Speech retrieval results were not yet available and are to be updated in a future version.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for multilingual speech representation learning, including training/fine-tuning and testing/validation of speech-only and speech-text pretrained models on ASR, speech translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval tasks. The paper encourages multilingual fine-tuning where applicable and specifies task-specific evaluation settings.
